- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). input.prompt:
Search this repository for authentication provider abstractions related to third-party identity providers (like OAuth, SAML, OIDC, SSO). I need to find:
1. Which package defines the provider abstraction (interface/abstract class for identity providers)
2. Which concrete protocol implementation package ships (e.g., OIDC, SAML, OAuth)

Search breadth: very thorough. Look in package names, directory structures, and key files. Try searching for terms like "provider", "identity", "auth", "oauth", "oidc", "saml", "sso" in package.json files, directory names, and source files. Report exact package names and file paths.

content.text:
That is just a comment reference, not an OIDC implementation. Here are the complete findings.

---

## Findings

This is the **usememos/memos** project (Go module `github.com/usememos/memos`). It has a clear two-layer identity provider architecture: a shared data-type package that defines the provider abstraction, and a single concrete protocol implementation package for OAuth2.

### 1. Provider Abstraction Package: `internal/idp`

**File:** `/bench/repo/internal/idp/idp.go`
**Go import path:** `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp`

This package defines the shared data structure that all identity provider implementations must produce:

```go
type IdentityProviderUserInfo struct {
    Identifier  string
    DisplayName string
    Email       string
    AvatarURL   string
}
```

This struct acts as the abstraction boundary. It is the common return type that any identity provider implementation must populate and return. The codebase does not define a Go `interface` with method signatures; instead it uses this shared struct as the contract -- concrete providers produce an `*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo`, and all consumer code (SSO login, identity linking) depends only on this type.

The protobuf layer also defines the type system for identity providers, with an extensible `oneof` pattern:

**File:** `/bench/repo/proto/store/idp.proto`
- `IdentityProvider` message with `Type` enum (currently: `OAUTH2 = 1`)
- `IdentityProviderConfig` message using `oneof config` (currently: `OAuth2Config oauth2_config = 1`)

**File:** `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/idp_service.proto`
- Defines the `IdentityProviderService` gRPC service (CRUD operations for identity providers)
- Mirrors the store-layer protobuf types for the API surface

### 2. Concrete Protocol Implementation: OAuth2 (the only one shipped)

**Package directory:** `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/`
**Go import path:** `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp/oauth2`
**Files:**
- `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` -- implementation
- `/bench/repo/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2_test.go` -- tests

This package provides:
- `IdentityProvider` struct (configured with `*storepb.OAuth2Config`)
- `NewIdentityProvider(config *storepb.OAuth2Config) (*IdentityProvider, error)` -- constructor with config validation
- `ExchangeToken(ctx, redirectURL, code, codeVerifier string) (string, error)` -- authorization code exchange (with PKCE support)
- `UserInfo(ctx, token string) (*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo, error)` -- fetches user info from the provider's userinfo endpoint and maps fields using configurable `FieldMapping`

It depends on `golang.org/x/oauth2` (at v0.36.0 per go.mod) for the token exchange.

### 3. No SAML, OIDC, or other protocol implementations exist

The codebase has **no** SAML, OIDC, or other identity protocol implementations. The only subdirectory under `/bench/repo/internal/idp/` is `oauth2/`. The protobuf `Type` enum only defines `OAUTH2 = 1`. The `oneof config` in `IdentityProviderConfig` only has `oauth2_config`. A grep for "saml", "oidc", and "openid" across all Go and proto files yielded only a single comment in `auth_service.proto` mentioning OIDC in passing ("Similar to OIDC's /userinfo endpoint").

### 4. Key supporting files

| Layer | File | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| Store | `/bench/repo/store/idp.go` | Persistence layer for identity providers (CRUD, config serialization) |
| Store DB drivers | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/idp.go`, `.../postgres/idp.go`, `.../mysql/idp.go` | Database-specific identity provider storage |
| API service | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/idp_service.go` | gRPC service implementing `IdentityProviderService` |
| SSO auth flow | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go` | SSO sign-in logic: resolves identity provider, exchanges token, resolves/creates user, links identities |
| User identities | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_identities.go` | Manages linked identities (list/create/get/delete linked SSO accounts per user) |
| Auth core | `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go` | Core authentication (session tokens, JWT) -- separate from IDP |
